<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518913912_theRebbe_602" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518913912_theRebbe_602__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This explains that the shofar's simple sound reflects the essential bond between the essence of the soul and the Essence (Atzmus), which is beyond letters and limitations.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And this will be understood based on the known concept that the reason the shofar blast is specifically a simple sound is because on Rosh HaShanah it is "to pass you through the covenant of Havayah your G-d,"</t>
    <t s="1">for this covenant is the essential bond between the Holy One, blessed be He, and Yisrael</t>
    <t s="2">(who passed together between the pieces)</t>
    <t s="3">to become truly one entity.</t>
    <t s="4">And since this bond is the bond of the essence of the soul with the Essence (Atzmus),</t>
    <t s="5">the simplicity of the essence of the soul with the simplicity of the Essence (Atzmus),</t>
    <t s="6">therefore the remembrance of the covenant and the bond is also specifically through a simple sound</t>
    <t s="7">(which is not clothed in letters),</t>
    <t s="8">for letters</t>
    <t s="9">(even the most sublime letters)</t>
    <t s="10">are limitation,</t>
    <t s="11">and the remembrance of the covenant and the bond of the simplicity of the essence of the soul with the simplicity of the Essence (Atzmus) is specifically through a simple sound.</t>
    <t s="12">And this is the meaning of the parable for the shofar blast, of the king's son who even forgot language,</t>
    <t s="13">for this forgetting is a virtue.</t>
    <t s="14">For since letters</t>
    <t s="15">(language)</t>
    <t s="16">are limiting,</t>
    <t s="17">therefore in order to come and reach the aspect of simplicity, one must forget language.</t>
    <t s="18">And analogous to the statement of Reish Lakish,</t>
    <t s="19">who fasted one hundred</t>
    <t s="20">fasts to forget the Babylonian Talmud so that he could learn the Jerusalem Talmud,</t>
    <t s="21">and analogous to the pillar that is between the Garden of Eden of the lower [world] and the Garden of Eden of the upper [world], whose function is</t>
    <t s="22">(as explained in Torah Ohr)</t>
    <t s="23">the forgetting and nullification of the comprehension and vision of the lower Garden of Eden,</t>
    <t s="24">for then specifically can one receive the revelation of the upper Garden of Eden.</t>
    <t s="25">And as it is in the Garden of Eden, that the comprehension of the lower Garden of Eden confuses the comprehension of the upper Garden of Eden,</t>
    <t s="26">so too is it</t>
    <t s="27">(and all the more so)</t>
    <t s="28">regarding the revelation of the aspect of simplicity that is entirely beyond comprehension,</t>
    <t s="29">for the entire matter of comprehension</t>
    <t s="30">(even the most sublime comprehension)</t>
    <t s="31">confuses the revelation of the aspect of simplicity.</t>
    <t s="32">And analogous to what is explained in Atteres Rosh</t>
    <t s="33">regarding the reason for the opinion that</t>
    <t s="34">commandments do not require intention</t>
    <t s="35">(meaning that the fulfillment of commandments must be with acceptance of the yoke, without reason or intention),</t>
    <t s="36">for seemingly it is astonishing, what does it matter to us if one also adds intention,</t>
    <t s="37">and he explains there,</t>
    <t s="38">that intention causes a diminution of light, so to speak, in the very acceptance of the yoke of the commandments, which is not so much in the manner of a yoke.</t>
    <t s="39">For the intention</t>
    <t s="40">(and reason)</t>
    <t s="41">of the commandment,</t>
    <t s="42">even at the most sublime level,</t>
    <t s="43">is within the category of attribute, depiction, and limitation,</t>
    <t s="44">unlike the commandment that is in the manner of acceptance of the yoke, whose root is in the simple Will and Pleasure,</t>
    <t s="45">and reason weakens, so to speak, the force and clarity of the essence of the commandment.</t>
    <t s="46">And from this it is also understood regarding the matter of the simple sound of the shofar blast,</t>
    <t s="47">that there must be forgetting and nullification of language,</t>
    <t s="48">for through this specifically one reaches the aspect of simplicity.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the second parable of simple garments, showing that to connect with G-d's Essence beyond the level of King, one must nullify even the garments of mitzvos.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">9)</t>
    <t s="1">And so too is it regarding the second parable,</t>
    <t s="2">the matter of garments,</t>
    <t s="3">for garments, even though they are for honor and glory,</t>
    <t s="4">like royal garments</t>
    <t s="5">(and likewise precious garments in general),</t>
    <t s="6">are within measurement and limitation.</t>
    <t s="7">For behold,</t>
    <t s="8">(in the analogue)</t>
    <t s="9">the garments are the matter of Torah and mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="10">for mitzvos are garments, as explained in Tanya,</t>
    <t s="11">and as is also understood from what the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Avraham Avinu, "Come, clothe yourself in My garments,"</t>
    <t s="12">and also Torah is a garment, as it is written,</t>
    <t s="13">"Havayah has donned strength, He has girded Himself," and there is no strength but Torah.</t>
    <t s="14">And since the service of Rosh HaShanah is the bond of Yisrael with His very Essence (Atzmus) as He is above the aspect of King</t>
    <t s="15">(for on Rosh HaShanah one must make Him King,</t>
    <t s="16">"Make Me King over you"),</t>
    <t s="17">and all the more so above the matter of decrees</t>
    <t s="18">(which come after He has already become King),</t>
    <t s="19">behold, in order to reach this, there must be a nullification of the garments of mitzvos</t>
    <t s="20">(in the manner explained above regarding the forgetting and nullification of language).</t>
    <t s="21">Therefore the parable for the shofar blast is specifically about simple garments,</t>
    <t s="22">for these garments indicate the bond with His very Essence (Atzmus) as He is above the aspect of King,</t>
    <t s="23">as he elaborates in the parable that these garments are like when the king was in the forest before he was restored to his royal throne,</t>
    <t s="24">and also in the analogue he explains that these garments are the matter of the garment that existed at the time of the Giving of the Torah, when we coronated Him with the shofar before the actual Giving of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="25">meaning before</t>
    <t s="26">(above)</t>
    <t s="27">He became King.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section clarifies that the seemingly unflattering language in the parable is actually a great praise, following the approach of the holy R. Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev who always judges Israel favorably.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">And although the expressions stated there</t>
    <t s="2">(in the parable and also in the analogue)</t>
    <t s="3">as they are literally, do not speak of the praise of Yisrael,</t>
    <t s="4">behold, it is stated in the maamar there that this parable is from the holy gaon, the chassid, Mahari"tz of Berditchev,</t>
    <t s="5">and it is known and famous in all the worlds that the holy R. Levi Yitzchak was a lover of Yisrael and an advocate for each and every one of Yisrael, tipping the scales for each and every one of Yisrael to the side of merit, and in a manner that is a priori,</t>
    <t s="6">and therefore,</t>
    <t s="7">when it says in the maamar that this parable is from the holy R. Levi Yitzchak,</t>
    <t s="8">it is simply understood that all the expressions stated there are for virtue.</t>
    <t s="9">And this is his method and his way regarding the children of Yisrael,</t>
    <t s="10">as is known the interpretation of the holy R. Levi Yitzchak on the verses at the beginning of the book of Yeshayahu,</t>
    <t s="11">where there are descriptions of the children of Yisrael that are seemingly [negative],</t>
    <t s="12">and the holy tzaddik of Berditchev interprets that these descriptions indicate their praise</t>
    <t s="13">[and as is also proven from the fact that these descriptions were stated in the book of Yeshayahu,</t>
    <t s="14">for Yeshayahu is a prophet of salvation,</t>
    <t s="15">as his name Yeshayahu is from the word yeshuah (salvation)],</t>
    <t s="16">and furthermore, they are the most sublime praises, unparalleled by any other praises.</t>
    <t s="17">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="18">based on the known concept</t>
    <t s="19">in the explanation of the Sages' statement,</t>
    <t s="20">"A person is punished with his knowledge and without his knowledge"</t>
    <t s="21">(and likewise in the explanation of the Mishnaic phrase</t>
    <t s="22">"judgment and accounting"),</t>
    <t s="23">that when a person states the verdict of another person, he thereby also judges himself,</t>
    <t s="24">behold, the verdict of the holy tzaddik of Berditchev regarding the aforementioned descriptions in Yeshayahu is also a verdict regarding the aforementioned descriptions in his Torah teachings and parables.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
